issues.description: Milkable.messageOnMilk(): The problem statement contains conflicting signatures for messageOnMilk(): the UML interface declaration in the problem statement indicates messageOnMilk(): boolean (problem_statement.md lines 51-53) and the textual instruction in Part 2 says it should return true/false (problem_statement.md lines 92-95), but the UML entries for Seal and Goat in the same problem statement show messageOnMilk(): String (problem_statement.md lines 31-35). The solution repository implements the Milkable interface with signature String messageOnMilk() (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java line 5) and Seal/Goat implement messageOnMilk() returning String (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Seal.java lines 19-20 and src/de/tum/cit/ase/Goat.java lines 15-17). This mismatch leaves students unsure whether to implement messageOnMilk() to return a boolean success flag or a descriptive String, and will cause compilation errors if students follow the problem text but the tests/solution expect the alternate signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the messageOnMilk() return type across all artifacts. Recommended: keep String (matches the solution). Update problem_statement.md so the Milkable interface and any UML entries for Seal/Goat declare messageOnMilk(): String and change the textual instruction in Part 2 to state that implementations should return a descriptive milking message (e.g., "Goat <name> is milked"). Alternatively, if boolean is preferred, change the solution and template to declare messageOnMilk(): boolean and update all implementations/tests to return boolean. Ensure UML diagrams, textual descriptions, template stubs, and tests all use the same signature.
